evals.prompt: fmt.nvim/ is my Neovim plugin. plugin/fmt.lua requires the main module at the top and then defines :Fmt. Users say it adds noticeable startup time even when they never run :Fmt. Fix it and show that it worked.
evals.expected_output: plugin/fmt.lua only defines :Fmt (keeping range = '%') and the callback requires 'fmt' itself, so the module loads on first use; proof via --startuptime or package.loaded in an isolated headless run.

assertions.text: plugin/fmt.lua has no top-level require of the plugin's own module.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import re; s = open("fmt.nvim/plugin/fmt.lua").read(); assert not re.search(r"^(local\s+\w+\s*=\s*)?require\s*\(?\s*[\x27\x22]fmt", s, re.M), s'

assertions.text: In an isolated headless Neovim (needs nvim or $NVIM), :Fmt exists after startup while package.loaded.fmt is still nil, and running :Fmt loads the module.
assertions.check: n="${NVIM:-nvim}"; command -v "$n" >/dev/null || { echo "nvim not found (set NVIM)"; exit 2; }; x=$(mktemp -d); XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$x/c" XDG_DATA_HOME="$x/d" XDG_STATE_HOME="$x/s" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$x/k" "$n" --clean --headless -i NONE --cmd "set rtp^=$PWD/fmt.nvim" -c 'lua local okc, err = pcall(function() local before = package.loaded.fmt == nil and vim.fn.exists([[:Fmt]]) == 2; vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, false, {[[a = 1]], [[bb = 2]]}); vim.cmd([[Fmt]]); ok = before and package.loaded.fmt ~= nil end); if not okc then io.stdout:write(tostring(err)) end; vim.cmd(okc and ok and [[qa!]] or [[cq]])'; rc=$?; rm -rf "$x"; exit $rc

assertions: The reply shows startup evidence from an isolated run (for example --startuptime lines mentioning fmt, or package.loaded before and after) or states exactly which command to run if Neovim was unavailable.
The :Fmt command keeps its range behavior (range = '%' or equivalent) and the implementation module is unchanged apart from what the fix needs.

evals.prompt: tidy.nvim/lua/tidy/init.lua pipes the buffer through `tidy -q` with vim.system. Sometimes it replaces the wrong buffer (when I switch buffers while it runs), sometimes it wipes out text I typed while tidy was running, and if I :bwipeout the buffer before tidy finishes I get an error. Also a failing tidy replaces my buffer with nothing. Fix all of it and add a headless test. The plugin supports Neovim 0.10+.
evals.expected_output: run() captures the buffer handle and changedtick before starting; the callback (via vim.schedule) checks nvim_buf_is_valid, the changedtick, and the exit code before replacing lines; vim.system start errors are caught with pcall and reported with vim.notify; a headless test covers the stale-edit and wiped-buffer cases.

assertions.text: The callback no longer writes to buffer 0, and the module checks nvim_buf_is_valid and changedtick.
assertions.check: ! grep -Eq 'nvim_buf_set_lines\(0' tidy.nvim/lua/tidy/init.lua && grep -q 'nvim_buf_is_valid' tidy.nvim/lua/tidy/init.lua && grep -q 'changedtick' tidy.nvim/lua/tidy/init.lua

assertions.text: The module checks the process exit code before applying output.
A Lua test file was added under tidy.nvim/.

assertions: The code does not use APIs newer than Neovim 0.10 (for example positional vim.validate from 0.11 or the `buf` key from 0.12), or guards them; quote any version-sensitive call.

The test forces the ordering (a buffer edit or wipe while the job is pending, then waiting on a condition with vim.wait) rather than relying on timing luck, and the reply says whether it actually ran.

evals.prompt: After I :source mdlint.nvim/plugin/mdlint.lua a second time (or my plugin manager reloads it), every save of a Markdown file runs the linter twice. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The autocmd is created in an augroup made with nvim_create_augroup('mdlint', { clear = true }) (group passed to nvim_create_autocmd), so re-sourcing replaces instead of adding; verified by counting BufWritePost autocmds after sourcing twice.

assertions.text: plugin/mdlint.lua creates an augroup with clear = true and passes it to the autocmd.
assertions.check: grep -Eq 'nvim_create_augroup' mdlint.nvim/plugin/mdlint.lua && grep -Eq 'clear[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*true' mdlint.nvim/plugin/mdlint.lua && grep -Eq 'group[[:space:]]*=' mdlint.nvim/plugin/mdlint.lua

assertions.text: In an isolated headless Neovim (needs nvim or $NVIM), sourcing plugin/mdlint.lua again does not add BufWritePost autocmds.
assertions.check: n="${NVIM:-nvim}"; command -v "$n" >/dev/null || { echo "nvim not found (set NVIM)"; exit 2; }; x=$(mktemp -d); XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$x/c" XDG_DATA_HOME="$x/d" XDG_STATE_HOME="$x/s" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$x/k" "$n" --clean --headless -i NONE --cmd "set rtp^=$PWD/mdlint.nvim" -c 'lua local okc, err = pcall(function() local a = #vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds({event = [[BufWritePost]]}); vim.cmd([[runtime! plugin/mdlint.lua]]); vim.cmd([[runtime! plugin/mdlint.lua]]); local b = #vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds({event = [[BufWritePost]]}); print(a, b); ok = a == b end); if not okc then io.stdout:write(tostring(err)) end; vim.cmd(okc and ok and [[qa!]] or [[cq]])'; rc=$?; rm -rf "$x"; exit $rc

assertions: The reply explains that nvim_create_autocmd adds a new handler on each run and that clearing the plugin's own group (not all BufWritePost autocmds) is the fix.

evals.prompt: notes.nvim/plugin/notes.lua maps <leader>n directly, which clobbers other people's mappings. Give users a proper way to trigger require('notes').open_today() from a key of their choice and update the help file. The plugin targets Neovim 0.12.
evals.expected_output: plugin/notes.lua defines a <Plug>(...) mapping (and keeps :NotesToday) without mapping <leader>n; doc/notes.txt documents the <Plug> mapping with an example vim.keymap.set('n', '<leader>n', '<Plug>(NotesToday)').

assertions.text: plugin/notes.lua no longer maps a <leader> key and defines a <Plug> mapping.
In an isolated headless Neovim (needs nvim or $NVIM), <leader>n is unmapped, a normal-mode <Plug> mapping exists, and :NotesToday still exists.
assertions.check: n="${NVIM:-nvim}"; command -v "$n" >/dev/null || { echo "nvim not found (set NVIM)"; exit 2; }; x=$(mktemp -d); XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$x/c" XDG_DATA_HOME="$x/d" XDG_STATE_HOME="$x/s" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$x/k" "$n" --clean --headless -i NONE --cmd "set rtp^=$PWD/notes.nvim" -c 'lua local okc, err = pcall(function() local plug = vim.tbl_filter(function(m) return m.lhs:find([[<Plug>]], 1, true) ~= nil end, vim.api.nvim_get_keymap([[n]])); ok = vim.fn.maparg([[<leader>n]], [[n]]) == [[]] and #plug > 0 and vim.fn.exists([[:NotesToday]]) == 2 end); if not okc then io.stdout:write(tostring(err)) end; vim.cmd(okc and ok and [[qa!]] or [[cq]])'; rc=$?; rm -rf "$x"; exit $rc

assertions: The help text shows how a user maps their own key to the <Plug> mapping, and the reply does not claim :helptags or :help was run unless the transcript shows it.

evals.prompt: trail.nvim/ only works if users call require('trail').setup(): setup() creates the command and autocmds, so people who forget it get nothing, calling it twice duplicates the autocmds, and a typo like setup({ timout = 10 }) is silently ignored. Restructure the configuration so it works with no setup call at all, can also be configured through a global variable, and reports bad or unknown options. Keep Neovim 0.11 support.
evals.expected_output: A plugin/trail.lua defines :TrailStrip and the autocmds in a cleared augroup without requiring setup; setup() only stores and validates options; configuration merges defaults, vim.g.trail, and setup() options, resolved lazily; unknown keys produce a vim.notify warning naming the key; wrong types are reported.

assertions.text: A plugin/ file exists and :TrailStrip is available without calling setup() (checked in an isolated headless Neovim; needs nvim or $NVIM).
assertions.check: test -f trail.nvim/plugin/trail.lua || { echo "no plugin/trail.lua"; exit 1; }; n="${NVIM:-nvim}"; command -v "$n" >/dev/null || { echo "nvim not found (set NVIM)"; exit 2; }; x=$(mktemp -d); XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$x/c" XDG_DATA_HOME="$x/d" XDG_STATE_HOME="$x/s" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$x/k" "$n" --clean --headless -i NONE --cmd "set rtp^=$PWD/trail.nvim" -c 'lua local okc, err = pcall(function() ok = vim.fn.exists([[:TrailStrip]]) == 2 end); if not okc then io.stdout:write(tostring(err)) end; vim.cmd(okc and ok and [[qa!]] or [[cq]])'; rc=$?; rm -rf "$x"; exit $rc

assertions.text: Calling setup() twice does not add TextChanged autocmds, and setup({ timout = 10 }) is reported through vim.notify at WARN or above or through an error (isolated headless Neovim; needs nvim or $NVIM).
assertions.check: n="${NVIM:-nvim}"; command -v "$n" >/dev/null || { echo "nvim not found (set NVIM)"; exit 2; }; x=$(mktemp -d); XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$x/c" XDG_DATA_HOME="$x/d" XDG_STATE_HOME="$x/s" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$x/k" "$n" --clean --headless -i NONE --cmd "set rtp^=$PWD/trail.nvim" -c 'lua local okc, err = pcall(function() local seen = false; vim.notify = function(msg, lvl) if (lvl or 0) >= vim.log.levels.WARN then seen = true end end; local t = require([[trail]]); pcall(t.setup, {}); local a = #vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds({event = [[TextChanged]]}); pcall(t.setup, {}); local b = #vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds({event = [[TextChanged]]}); local okset = pcall(t.setup, {timout = 10}); if t.config then pcall(function() local _ = t.config.timeout end) end; ok = a == b and (seen or not okset) end); if not okc then io.stdout:write(tostring(err)) end; vim.cmd(okc and ok and [[qa!]] or [[cq]])'; rc=$?; rm -rf "$x"; exit $rc

assertions.text: The configuration reads a vim.g.trail table.

assertions: Unknown option keys are reported by name (for example 'trail: unknown option timout'), and type errors in known options are reported too; quote the code.
The README documents configuring without setup() (vim.g.trail) and that setup() is optional.

evals.prompt: Add a mapping to my Neovim config (nvim-config/init.lua) so <leader>w saves the file. That's all.
evals.expected_output: One line in init.lua such as vim.keymap.set('n', '<leader>w', '<cmd>write<cr>', { desc = 'Save file' }); no plugin structure, tests, or <Plug> mapping.

assertions.text: init.lua maps <leader>w in normal mode to a write command.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import re; s = open("nvim-config/init.lua").read(); assert re.search(r"keymap\.set\(\s*[\x27\x22]n[\x27\x22]\s*,\s*[\x27\x22]<leader>w[\x27\x22]\s*,[^\n]*(write|:w\b|update)", s, re.I), s'

assertions.text: No plugin/ or lua/ directories, tests, or <Plug> mappings were created.
assertions.check: test -z "$(find . -path ./.claude -prune -o -type d \( -name plugin -o -name lua -o -name tests \) -print)" && ! grep -q '<Plug>' nvim-config/init.lua
